key_insight: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively fingerprint specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films and quantify them via spectral oscillator strength.
engineering_relevance: This enables closed-loop defect diagnostics and passivation for higher-efficiency, more stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of device-relevant perovskite thin films.
Match intrinsic phonon and defect-localized vibrational signatures across a THz fingerprint library.
Use oscillator-strength changes as a quantitative defect metric to guide passivation and quality control.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct defect meter.
watch_item: Fingerprint specificity and calibration may depend on composition, film morphology, and the availability of a well-validated THz reference library.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
